title: Fusion Commit + On-Demand Burst Pricing experiment for Dedicated GPU Pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Run a controlled experiment of a hybrid pricing product were calling 'Fusion Commit' that blends limited-duration reserved commitments with an on-demand surge credit pool. Objective is to improve ARR predictability for enterprise customers while increasing utilization and overage revenue without increasing churn.

Background: Sales and CS report that customers want cheaper baseline capacity but fear long-term lockups. Engineering can offer finer-grained autoscale with minutes-level preemption and SLAs differentiated by band. Existing experiments focus on slab and elastic reserves; Fusion Commit reframes the product as a blended contract: a committed baseline (monthly GPU-hours), an attached flexible credit pool (Fusion Credits) that customers consume when demand spikes, and optional SLA bands (Gold/Silver/Bronze) that guarantee latency and preemption windows.

Hypothesis: Offering a Fusion Commit plan with a modest discount on baseline reserved hours (10-18%), bundled Fusion Credits (for burst), and explicit SLA bands will: (1) increase conversion for mid-enterprise customers (>=$20k MRR) by lowering perceived commitment risk, (2) increase net GPU utilization by absorbing burst demand into Fusion Credits rather than unmanaged on-demand, and (3) improve overall ARR predictability by increasing committed baseline retention.

Scope: Experiment is collection & pricing design, contract and SOW template updates, Console UX for showing Fusion Credit balance, billing & metering changes, and legal/security questionnaire updates for the blended contract. Not in scope: changes to underlying autoscaler algorithms beyond tagging/reservation semantics.

Acceptance criteria: Will promote to pilot if all of the following by pilot end (90d): (1) >=15% of targeted accounts accept Fusion Commit versus standard reserved SKU, (2) churn velocity for participating accounts is <= baseline churn, (3) net revenue per GPU-hour (inc overage) improves by >=5% vs current reserved + on-demand mix, (4) no unresolved legal or security blockers for enterprise contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Net revenue per GPU-hour +5% vs baseline
Legal/security questionnaire signoff for pilot contracts
success_metrics: Latency SLO miss rate on gold band (%)
Rate of overage bill disputes per 100 invoices
experiment_plan: 1) Pricing matrix design & model (2 weeks): produce 3 pricing variants (Aggressive, Balanced, Conservative) with per-GPU-hour math, sample contracts, and sample customer bill backs. 2) Legal & Security Q: update SQ template with Fusion Credit terms, preemption policies, and audit obligations (1 week). 3) Engineering & Billing: implement metering tag for Fusion Credits, UI card in Console, and invoice line items (4 weeks). 4) Sales pilot (8 accounts) + Customer Success enablement (6 weeks). 5) Telemetry & dashboards: allocate Grafana/Console dashboards and define queries (1 week).
sample_pricing_table: Variant: Balanced — Baseline discount 14% on committed hours, Fusion Credits = 20% of baseline at 60% discounted rate, Gold SLA add-on +15%
Variant: Aggressive — Baseline discount 18%, Fusion Credits = 30% at 55% discounted rate, Gold SLA add-on +20%
Variant: Conservative — Baseline discount 10%, Fusion Credits = 10% at 70% discounted rate, Gold SLA add-on +12%
billing_and_metering_notes: Fusion Credits should be tracked as a separate balance with timestamped consumption records. Billing lines: committed baseline usage, fusion_credit_consumption, on_demand_overflow. Overage pricing flows to either charged on-demand rates or pre-negotiated uplift depending on SLA band. Need to ensure accurate proration for mid-cycle changes.
